The "ORGANIC" class label is not something I can trust over that. memos.scout:
The honest case for buying ROACH now is thin, and I'd lean toward skipping it.

What supports it: the coin is alive, classed ORGANIC with no airdrop dump seen, it has 1,688 buyers and about $104k of volume in the last 15 minutes, and net flow over that window is slightly positive (+2.55 SOL). It's up 72% over 30 minutes, the pool is deep at ~202 SOL, and early post-graduation buying (226 SOL from 361 buyers) was broad, with the top 5 buyers holding only 33%.

What argues against it: the 15-minute return is already -6.3%, the price is 23% off its 30-minute high, and sells nearly match buys (441 vs 444 SOL). The curve data is a warning sign: bundle_share is 1.0 and top-3 share is 86%, which suggests coordinated early accumulation rather than organic demand. Flow has already rolled over from the peak, and a 30-second execution delay plus 1.4-5.1% round-trip costs leave little room. Coins in this state usually keep fading rather than recovering.

Verdict: no strong case for buying now. Skip.
memos.skeptic:
Most likely loss: insider distribution after a fast run-up. The curve data shows bundle_share 1.0 and top3_share 0.86, meaning nearly all early supply sat with a few coordinated wallets, and completer_share 1.14 suggests the graduating buyers were concentrated enough that a few bundles can exit at will. Launch bot present, and the first 2 minutes post-graduation show sell_to_buy 0.76 with 361 buyers, so early flow was already net-selling into the pool.

The last 15 minutes are nearly flat in net flow (+2.55 SOL on 444 SOL bought), with return -6.3% and 389 sellers against 1,688 buyers. That is churn, not accumulation. The 23% drawdown from the 30-minute high, after a 72% gain, looks like the first leg of a distribution rather than a dip to buy.

With only 201.9 SOL of pool depth and a 1.4-5.1% round trip, a $20 ticket needs a clean move of roughly 5% to break even. Given the concentrated holders and sell pressure, I'd skip.
